preprocessing.operation: first difference independently within each file
preprocessing.normalization: no separate z-score, scaling, smoothing, clipping, or imputation; Pearson centers finite aligned observations internally

statistic.name: lagged_change_correlation_candidate_score
statistic.numerical_backend: NumPy float64 vectorized implementation with an independent math.fsum scalar parity oracle
statistic.horizon_eligibility: both train1 and train2 correlations finite, nonzero, and with the same sign
statistic.selected_horizon: strongest eligible horizon, with the shorter horizon winning an exact strength tie

directionality.explanation: The ordered candidate uses a frozen source role at t and a frozen target role at t+h. This temporal alignment is directional even though ordinary Pearson correlation on one fixed aligned vector pair is algebraically symmetric.
directionality.reverse_pair_semantics: Reversing source and target would create a different lag-alignment calculation and is not inferred from the forward result. In the frozen universe, source and target role sets are disjoint, so reverse-role candidates are not automatically present.
directionality.sign_semantics: positive or negative denotes the stable sign of lagged first-difference association across train1 and train2

ranking_and_budget.score_interpretation: cross-file stability strength for candidate ranking, not a probability or comparable cross-arm score

pseudocode: Load and self-validate the frozen C0 universe, budget, access, and STAT policies.
Bind train1 and train2 to verified manifest identities and normal-only structural evidence.
Run the synthetic vectorized-versus-scalar numerical parity gate before real file access.
Read each authorized file once as the exact ordered 24-column float64 matrix.
For each file independently, compute first differences for the 12 sources and 12 targets.
For each horizon in 1, 5, 10, 30, 60, correlate source differences through row -h with target differences from row +h.
For each ordered source-target pair, retain horizons whose two file correlations are finite, nonzero, and same-sign.
Select the eligible horizon with maximum minimum-absolute two-file correlation; break exact ties toward shorter horizon.
Rank supported pairs deterministically, then append unstable pairs for audit only.
Derive top10, top20, and top40 as prefixes without reranking or padding.
Freeze private evidence, public access audit, and sanitized public result; integration later consumes only the top20 pair identities and arm-local evidence binding.

candidate_observation.text: The frozen arm produced 20 primary STAT candidates from one deterministic supported ranking.

unknowns_and_limitations.item: The scientific rationale for choosing primary top-20, beyond the frozen common arm budget, is not documented in the audited STAT implementation.
unknowns_and_limitations.impact: future sensitivity or preregistration justification issue, not an implementation defect

unknowns_and_limitations.item: Two finite observations are mathematically accepted; the implementation intentionally has no support-count threshold beyond finiteness and nonzero variance.
